vibe.rationale: Vibe 4 — holding from July 18 evening's Vibe 4 for a fourth consecutive session. The July 19 session closes the 72-hour post-Hellfire-interdiction window — the most significant pending milestone identified in July 18 evening's watch list — without confirmed major Iranian kinetic escalation. The IRGC's explicit 'full-scale offensive operations if US attacks continue for another 2-3 days' ultimatum, issued July 15, has now lapsed without triggering. This 72h absence of confirmed major kinetic response is the single strongest Iranian restraint signal of the blockade phase, stronger than the 24h signal (July 17) and 48h signal (July 18). However, the IC's characterization of this restraint as strategic decision or operational pause remains the primary unresolved analytical question — and a Vibe 5 upgrade is contingent on that characterization, combined with Lebanon diplomatic progress, neither of which is confirmed as of July 19 evening. The session holds at Vibe 4 rather than upgrading to Vibe 5 on four structural grounds. First, the IC has not confirmed the 72h restraint as strategic restraint — Acting DNI Day 59 is delivering the characterization but it has not been publicly released or officially communicated to the market or diplomatic channels. Second, Lebanon pilot zones Day 3 definitively expired the Rome agreement's original 48-72h implementation window without confirmed IDF movement; Lebanon has explicitly threatened to skip future Rome talks if Israel does not fulfill its withdrawal pledge, raising the diplomatic fragility of the follow-on track. Hezbollah stand-down Day 34 holds — Iran is maintaining restraint guidance — but the factual predicate for Iran to declare MOU compliance progress has not materialized. Third, PNW wildfire activity materially escalated on July 19, invalidating July 18 evening's 'structural positive' assessment: the Kaiser Canyon Fire (Okanogan County / Colville Reservation) expanded to 2,170 acres with Level 3 evacuations at 0% containment, and the Franklin County fire complex reached approximately 38,000 acres near Kahlotus — both active without confirmed containment under the WA DNR burn ban (Day 3) and ahead of the July 21-24 heat wave peak. Fourth, the IRGC regional energy threat intent assessment — whether 'oil and gas for everyone or no one' reflects operational intent to attack GCC energy infrastructure or strategic signaling — remains unresolved, sustaining the oil market tail risk premium. Positive factor 1 (72h Iranian restraint window closes without confirmed major kinetic escalation): The IRGC has not confirmed a naval challenge to CENTCOM interdiction operations, an attack on Gulf partner energy infrastructure (Saudi Ras Tanura, UAE Fujairah, Qatar Ras Laffan, Kuwait crude terminals), or Hezbollah mobilization orders through 72 hours of the post-Hellfire window. The lapse of the IRGC's explicit 2-3-day escalation ultimatum without triggering is the primary structural positive of the blockade phase to date. Positive factor 2 (World Cup Final MetLife Stadium completed clean): The Argentina vs Spain FIFA World Cup 2026 Final at MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, NJ) — 82,000 in-stadium, 50+ million viewers — completed without confirmed security incident. The NIFC-FIFA co-response coordination (Day 22) successfully managed concurrent fire weather and mass-event emergency response through the final, with no confirmed fire weather incident affecting the event corridor. Positive factor 3 (CISA clean streak Day 79 — 72h Iranian cyber window closed clean): The 72-hour post-Hellfire-interdiction window — the highest-risk period for Iranian-affiliated offensive cyber activation given the IRGC's maximum incentive to respond — closed on July 19 without a confirmed CISA-reportable cyber incident targeting US critical infrastructure. The 79-day clean streak is sustained. Positive factor 4 (Section 301 Brazil 25% tariff finalized — partial execution): USTR announced a 25% tariff on certain Brazilian imports under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, effective July 22. While this is a country-specific action (not the full forced-labor framework), it demonstrates USTR's July 20-24 execution capacity ahead of Section 122 expiry. Negative factor 1 (Lebanon pilot zones Day 3 — Rome implementation window definitively expired; diplomatic track fragility elevated): The Rome agreement's original 48-72h implementation window definitively closed on July 19 without confirmed IDF movement in designated south Lebanon pilot zones. Lebanon publicly demanded Israel fulfill its withdrawal pledge or it would skip future Rome talks. The diplomatic track is not foreclosed — an expanded timeline or Paris channel could reopen it — but the July 16-19 implementation window failed to produce observable military movement that Iran requires as the factual predicate for suspending the Hormuz re-closure declaration. Iran's maintained Hezbollah stand-down (Day 34) signals continued diplomatic engagement preference, but the implementation timeline has slipped. Negative factor 2 (PNW wildfire escalation invalidates July 18 'structural positive'): Kaiser Canyon Fire (Okanogan County / Colville Reservation) has expanded to 2,170 acres with Level 3 evacuations expanded to include Rebecca Lake, Belvedere, Buffalo Lake Road, Joe Moses Road, and Nespelem areas, at 0% containment with approximately 200 firefighters deployed. The Franklin County fire complex (~38,000 acres near Kahlotus) is the largest new fire complex of the Eastern Washington burn ban period. Both fires are active without confirmed containment ahead of the July 21-24 heat wave peak (Eastern Washington forecast 90s-100°F+), creating maximum compound risk conditions for fire growth. Negative factor 3 (IRGC regional energy threat intent unresolved — IC primary question Day 59): The IC has not released an assessment of whether the IRGC 'oil and gas for everyone or no one' statement from July 16 reflects operational intent to attack GCC energy infrastructure or strategic signaling. This unresolved assessment sustains the oil market structural tail risk premium and prevents the clean Brent/WTI retracement that would signal a Vibe 5 pathway. Upgrade to Vibe 5 requires: IC formally characterizes 72h Iranian restraint as strategic restraint decision (not operational pause); AND either (a) confirmed concrete IDF movement in south Lebanon pilot zones with Lebanese Army control transfer that Iran publicly acknowledges as MOU clause satisfaction, OR (b) WTI retraces to below $76 / Brent below $82 on IC restraint-signal confirmation and diplomatic track extension. Drop to Vibe 3 requires: WTI above $85; confirmed IRGC kinetic activation against GCC energy infrastructure (Ras Tanura, Fujairah, Ras Laffan, Kuwait terminals); CENTCOM-IRGC direct naval engagement in Strait; Kharg Island struck; confirmed Iranian offensive cyber attack on US critical infrastructure; or Kaiser Canyon or Franklin County fire complex escalating to major complex with mass casualties under July 21-24 heat wave peak conditions.

items.summary: The 72-hour post-Hellfire-interdiction assessment window — the most significant pending milestone identified in July 18 evening's watch list — closed on July 19 without a confirmed major Iranian kinetic escalation. No confirmed IRGC naval challenge to CENTCOM interdiction operations, no confirmed IRGC attack on Gulf partner energy infrastructure (Saudi Ras Tanura, UAE Fujairah, Qatar Ras Laffan, Kuwait crude terminals), and no confirmed Hezbollah mobilization orders were reported through July 19 evening. Critically, the IRGC's explicit 'full-scale offensive operations if US attacks continue for another 2-3 days' ultimatum — the most specific escalation timeline any senior Iranian figure attached to the post-MOU July cycle — was issued July 15 and has now definitively lapsed without triggering the threatened response. The 72h restraint window closing is the strongest Iranian restraint signal of the blockade phase: the combined 72h absence of confirmed major kinetic response following the July 16 CENTCOM Hellfire interdiction of a commercial tanker — the most provocative enforcement action of the 2026 arc — materially alters the tail-risk probability assessment in the market and IC. The IC characterization of this 72h restraint — strategic decision not to escalate kinetically or operational pause while preparing a delayed response — remains the primary unresolved analytical task. Acting DNI Day 59 carries this characterization as the primary deliverable: a 'strategic restraint' conclusion is the primary factual predicate for a Vibe 5 upgrade; an 'operational pause' conclusion sustains Vibe 3-4 tail risk regardless of the market's modest price relief. Lebanon pilot zones Day 3: the original Rome agreement implementation window definitively expired on July 19 without confirmed IDF movement in designated south Lebanon pilot zones. Lebanon's demand escalated to an explicit threat: Beirut will skip future Rome talks if Israel does not fulfill its withdrawal pledge. An expanded timeline agreement negotiated through Rome, Paris, or a new diplomatic channel is required to restore implementation momentum. The SNSC formal MOU void declaration and Kharg Island strike remain the two un-activated escalatory rungs above current US posture. Hezbollah stand-down Day 34 continues through July 19 — Iran is maintaining restraint guidance pending diplomatic re-engagement rather than declaring the track failed.

items.summary: Four secondary geopolitical threads on July 19 evening. First: World Cup Final completed. The Argentina vs Spain FIFA World Cup 2026 Final at MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, NJ) — scheduled for 3 PM ET, approximately 82,000 in-stadium and 50+ million viewers — concluded on July 19. The largest concentrated US domestic security deployment of 2026 (DHS, Secret Service, FEMA in full event mode) concluded without a confirmed security incident at the venue or in the East Rutherford-New York corridor. NIFC-FIFA co-response coordination (Day 22) successfully managed concurrent fire weather and mass-event emergency response during peak fire season — a particularly demanding co-planning environment given the concurrent Kaiser Canyon Level 3 evacuations and Franklin County fire complex active during the Final. Second: Russia fuel crisis Day 19. Omsk refinery continues at 75% offline capacity with no restoration signal on Day 19. Ukraine drone strike tempo remains the primary x-factor for additional facility losses. By July 2026, 80 of 83 Russian regions are experiencing fuel restrictions affecting approximately 50 million people. Russia's crude processing rate fell to 3.91 million barrels per day in July 2026, down more than 1.4 million bpd from the prior year. Putin's mini-refinery decree (Euro-3 standard, 3-month construction timeline) and Mishustin's Euro-5 to Euro-3 quality downgrade authorization remain the only near-term domestic mitigation. IEA dual shock (Hormuz blockade Day 5 + Omsk Day 19) deepens. Third: Peru T-9. Keiko Fujimori's July 28 inauguration proceeds on track. Fourth: Colombia T-19. Abelardo De La Espriella's August 7 inauguration on track. Venezuela earthquake Day 26 (1,719+ confirmed dead, 46,600+ missing) with Maduro in New York federal custody — humanitarian access to earthquake-affected areas remains restricted.

items.summary: Oil markets on Blockade Day 5 registered a modest further relief movement on the 72-hour post-Hellfire-interdiction window closing without confirmed major Iranian kinetic escalation. WTI traded in the approximately $78-81 range on July 19 — down an additional $1-2 from July 18's $79-81 range — and Brent in the $83-86 range, pulling further below the $85 threshold. The combined 72h absence of confirmed IRGC kinetic response and the lapse of the explicit July 15 'full-scale offensive' ultimatum without triggering are materially reducing the immediate escalation premium. The primary remaining pricing driver is the unresolved IC assessment of whether the IRGC 'oil and gas for everyone or no one' statement reflects operational intent to attack GCC energy infrastructure. The market is maintaining a structural tail risk premium for the scenario in which the IC concludes this is operational intent rather than strategic signaling — a scenario that would convert the current Iran-specific supply disruption into a Gulf-wide energy closure (~20-25% of global oil and gas). Strait of Hormuz tanker transits remained at approximately 10% of pre-war baseline (approximately 1 tanker per day versus 55 pre-war) through July 19, confirming the strait is closed by operational reality. Federal Reserve Chair Warsh's rate path remained unchanged through July 19 — no FOMC communications on a Sunday. September rate hike odds holding at 68.8% and December at 85.3% reflect the market's assessment that Hormuz-era oil prices foreclose a September hold. The IEA dual shock deepens on Day 5 of the blockade and Day 19 of the Russia fuel crisis.

items.summary: Five secondary economic-legislative threads on July 19 evening. First: Section 301 partial execution. USTR announced and finalized a 25% tariff on certain Brazilian imports under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, effective July 22 — demonstrating USTR's capacity to execute Section 301 actions in the July 20-24 window. The broader forced-labor Section 301 framework (10% on 15 partners including EU, Canada, UK, Mexico; 12.5% on 46 countries) — the structural replacement for Section 122 emergency bridge authority — is expected by USTR before the Section 122 statutory expiry on July 24. No White House announcement of the forced-labor framework finalization was made through July 19 evening; the July 20 business-day deadline remains the primary target with Blockade Day 5 response assessment consuming White House bandwidth. Second: Section 122 T-5. Emergency tariff bridge authority expires July 24 — statutory, cannot be waived by executive action without congressional authorization. The 3-4 day compliance gap window (July 20-24) is live if USTR's forced-labor framework slips past July 20. Major importers with China/Vietnam/India exposure continue dual-track planning. All six ISO/RTOs (PJM, MISO, SPP, CAISO, ISO-NE, NYISO) must file generation adequacy reports by close of business Monday July 20 — the first legally required national accounting of AI-era data center large-load integration readiness. Fourth: OBBB Day 20. Medicaid work requirements and SNAP restrictions in 18 states, zero federal stays, CBO $3.4 trillion 10-year deficit projection — no new OBBB developments on July 19. items.summary: The July 19 PNW fire domain materially escalates from July 18 evening's 'structural positive' assessment. Three primary infrastructure events. First: Kaiser Canyon Fire active with Level 3 evacuations. The Kaiser Canyon Fire, ignited July 16 by lightning on the Colville Reservation in Okanogan County, expanded to 2,170 acres by July 19 evening with 0% containment. Level 3 'Go Now' evacuations were expanded to include Rebecca Lake, Belvedere, Buffalo Lake Road, Joe Moses Road, and Nespelem to Jackson Ranch on the south side of State Route 15. Approximately 200 firefighters are engaged in direct attack suppression using hand crews, brush trucks, air support, and dozers. The fire is moving north and northeast. A power outage in Okanogan County is associated with fire-related infrastructure impacts. The Kaiser Canyon Fire represents the first active Level 3 evacuation fire of the Eastern Washington burn ban period, invalidating the July 18 evening 'structural positive' (no new Level 2+ fires through July 18 weekend). Second: Franklin County fire complex. Approximately 38,000 acres of fires near Kahlotus in Franklin County represent the largest new fire complex of the burn ban period, sparked by the July 16 lightning outbreak. Third: Sourdough Fire Day 15. Extended attack status in North Cascades NP continues with SR-20 open and the Skagit River dam complex (Gorge/Diablo/Ross hydropower) in continuing restoration. The B and O Fire remains at 100% containment (Day 9 post-containment). Sourdough continues as the only pre-existing IMT-managed fire in extended attack. NIFC PL4 Day 21 sustained nationally. FERC AI generation adequacy reports are due Monday July 20 — the Pacific Northwest footprint (BPA/CAISO/Northwest Power Pool with the Microsoft Quincy/Wenatchee campus, Amazon BPA data center footprint, and Google The Dalles/Malheur corridor) is the most scrutinized regional grid. BPA grid stable.

items.summary: Four secondary infrastructure threads on July 19 evening. First: Washington drought Day 45. The fourth consecutive drought year continues with NOAA's Super El Niño development forecast extending warm and dry anomalies through September-October. Columbia River Basin remains the federal drought outlook's most likely western intensification zone for the next three-month window. Late-July heat wave building toward the July 21-24 peak (Portland upper 80s to low 90s; Eastern Washington 90s-100°F+) creates maximum compound conditions for fire growth and power demand against drought-reduced Columbia River hydropower output. The Kaiser Canyon and Franklin County fires are now active under these conditions. Second: Geomagnetic storm tail declining. The G4-class storm's K-index has continued to decline from the July 17 peak through July 19. Aurora borealis remains potentially visible across Washington state on clear nights — particularly north of I-90 — but activity is diminishing. BPA GIC monitoring at high-latitude transformer installations is winding down from peak vigilance; no GIC events causing grid disruption confirmed through July 19 evening. Third: NSF Newport OR Dark Day 21. Senate reinstallation authorization unanimous; physical reinstallation timeline pending congressional scheduling. Two active fires without the Newport coastal atmospheric anchor (Kaiser Canyon Day 4 + Sourdough Day 15 — increased from one with the Kaiser Canyon escalation on July 19). Newport dark status entering its fourth week. Fourth: BPA summer peak load management. The late-July heat wave entering its demand-growth acceleration phase against below-normal Columbia River streamflow and Skagit dam complex at partial restoration capacity. BPA's Bonneville-to-California transmission corridor is at normal operational status.

items.summary: Four primary domestic governance threads on July 19 evening. First: Acting DNI Day 59 — primary IC deliverable day. The IC's primary analytical task on July 19 is the 72-hour post-Hellfire-interdiction characterization: the IC must now formally assess whether the 72h absence of confirmed major Iranian kinetic escalation reflects (a) strategic restraint — Iran has made a strategic decision not to escalate kinetically in response to the Hellfire interdiction, materially reducing the tail risk premium — or (b) an operational pause — Iran is preparing a delayed kinetic response and the 72h quiet period reflects preparation rather than decision. This IC characterization is the most consequential analytical product of the blockade phase and the primary gating factor for a Vibe 5 upgrade: a restraint conclusion is the factual predicate for oil market relief and diplomatic pathway reopening; an operational-pause conclusion sustains the Vibe 3 tail risk regardless of market signals. Acting DNI simultaneously carries the IRGC regional energy threat intent evaluation (July 16 'oil and gas for everyone or no one' statement), the Lebanon pilot zones Day 3 assessment (Rome window expiry implications; Iran's signal via Hezbollah stand-down Day 34 maintenance), and Iranian offensive cyber pre-positioning evaluation. Fifty-nine consecutive days without Senate-confirmed IC leadership under the heaviest concurrent crisis load of the 2026 arc. Second: CISA clean streak Day 79. The 72-hour post-Hellfire-interdiction window — the highest-risk period for Iranian-affiliated offensive cyber activation — closed on July 19 without a confirmed CISA-reportable incident targeting US critical infrastructure. The clean streak is sustained at Day 79. The IRGC's maximum offensive cyber incentive window has now passed without activation. Third: NDAA blocked Day 4 (July 15 50-46 cloture failure). No path to Senate reconsideration announced through July 19. The defense authorization failure during active US military engagement remains a historic institutional gap. Fourth: OBBB Day 20. No new OBBB judicial or legislative developments on July 19.

items.summary: Four secondary domestic threads on July 19 evening. First: Measles CDC update confirmed. The CDC's July 16 measles update — noted as overdue in July 18 evening's brief — has been confirmed at 2,260 cases through July 16, 2026. This represents 29 new cases from the prior count (2,231 through July 9) and sustains the CIDRAP slowing signal (now Day 43 of weekly deceleration). The confirmed CDC update modestly revises the Seafair convergence monitoring picture: the July 23 expected next update now falls on T-4 from today, coinciding with Seafair Fleet Week start (July 21-24, approximately 500,000 attendance) and the measles tertiary monitoring window opening (July 23-26). Georgetown University wastewater surveillance and King and Snohomish County emergency department monitoring remain the primary early-detection mechanisms through the Seafair-tertiary convergence. No new clusters confirmed in King or Snohomish counties through July 19. Second: EAC all members relieved Day 10. Ten consecutive days without a functioning Election Assistance Commission — no replacement members nominated or announced through July 19. Third: Maine Democratic Party replacement candidate deadline T-8 (July 27). No candidate has confirmed through July 19 — fundraising window effectively closed. items.summary: The July 19 PNW fire and health session represents a material deterioration from July 18 evening's 'structural positive' framing. The WA DNR burn ban (Day 3) now overlaps with two active fire fronts for the first time of the burn ban period: the Kaiser Canyon Fire (Okanogan County / Colville Reservation, 2,170 acres, Level 3 evacuations, 0% containment, lighting-caused July 16) and the Franklin County fire complex (~38,000 acres near Kahlotus, July 16 lightning origin). Both fires are active without confirmed containment as the late-July heat wave builds toward its July 21-24 peak. The Kaiser Canyon Fire's expanded Level 3 evacuations — Rebecca Lake, Belvedere, Buffalo Lake Road, Joe Moses Road, and Nespelem to Jackson Ranch on the south side of SR-15 — represent the first mass-evacuation event of the Eastern Washington burn ban period. An associated Okanogan County power outage is infrastructure-grade. Approximately 200 firefighters are deployed on direct attack on Kaiser Canyon alone. Resources freed from B and O Fire demobilization (100% contained July 17) are available for redeployment and are the primary suppression capacity backstop for both active fronts. Sourdough Fire remains on extended attack (Day 15, North Cascades NP) with SR-20 open and Skagit River dam complex continuing restoration. NIFC PL4 Day 21 sustained nationally. BPA grid stable despite the Kaiser Canyon power outage (isolated to local distribution); heat wave demand build entering acceleration phase. Seafair Fleet Week is two days out — Parade of Ships through Elliott Bay on July 21, ship tours July 22-23, departure July 24; Blue Angels are July 31-August 2. The CDC measles update confirmed at 2,260 (July 16) resolves the prior 'overdue' status. The next CDC update (~July 23) will arrive on Seafair's opening day, coinciding with the measles tertiary monitoring window (July 23-26) — the brief's primary PNW health monitoring convergence, unchanged from prior sessions. Georgetown wastewater and King/Snohomish ED monitoring are the pre-Seafair early detection mechanisms through the July 23 convergence.

items.summary: Four secondary PNW environmental and regional threads on July 19 evening. First: geomagnetic storm tail declining. NOAA's G4-class severe geomagnetic storm has continued declining through July 19 — K-index falling further from the July 17 G4 peak. Aurora borealis remains potentially visible across Washington state on clear nights (particularly north of I-90), but activity is diminishing as the storm tail settles. BPA's GIC monitoring at high-latitude transformer installations is winding down from peak vigilance — no GIC events causing grid disruption confirmed through July 19. HF radio and GPS impacts are at below-G3 level and continuing to normalize. Second: NSF Newport OR ocean observatory Dark Day 21. Senate reinstallation authorization unanimous, physical reinstallation timeline pending congressional scheduling. Two active fires without the Newport coastal atmospheric baseline anchor (Kaiser Canyon Day 4 + Sourdough Day 15 — increased from one with the July 19 Kaiser Canyon escalation). Newport dark entering its fourth week. The Oregon fire monitoring dimension is degraded precisely as the wildfire season enters its most active period. Third: FERC AI T-0 nominal. All six ISO/RTOs must submit generation adequacy reports Monday July 20. The PNW-specific context remains the brief's highest-scrutiny entity: BPA, CAISO (Northwest import/export flows), and the Northwest Power Pool must account for the Microsoft Quincy/Wenatchee campus, Amazon BPA data center footprint, and Google The Dalles/Malheur corridor against the backdrop of drought-reduced hydropower output and the Kaiser Canyon power outage in the Okanogan corridor. Fourth: Columbia Basin drought heat convergence Day 45. Columbia River flow at Bonneville Dam continues below normal. The July 21-24 heat wave peak convergence with below-normal hydropower, Skagit dam partial restoration, Kaiser Canyon power outage, and two active uncontained fires creates the summer demand/supply/infrastructure convergence scenario BPA has been managing since early July — but materially more stressed on July 19 than July 18.

analyst_summary: July 19, 2026 evening holds at Vibe 4 — carrying forward from July 18 evening's Vibe 4 for a fourth consecutive session, defined by the 72-hour post-Hellfire-interdiction window closing without confirmed major Iranian kinetic escalation (the primary watch item of July 18 evening's brief, now resolved in the direction of restraint) and a material escalation in PNW wildfire activity (Kaiser Canyon Fire Level 3 evacuations; Franklin County complex ~38,000 acres) that invalidates July 18 evening's 'structural positive' assessment. The 72h restraint signal is the session's most significant single event: the combined absence of confirmed IRGC naval challenge, Gulf energy infrastructure attack, and Hezbollah mobilization orders through 72 hours of the post-interdiction window — combined with the lapse of the IRGC's explicit 'full-scale offensive if US attacks continue 2-3 days' ultimatum from July 15 — materially reduces the probability of a major delayed Iranian kinetic response and is the strongest restraint signal of the blockade phase. The IC's characterization of this restraint as strategic decision or operational pause is the primary pending analytical product that will determine the next vibe movement: a 'strategic restraint' conclusion from Acting DNI (Day 59) is the gating factor for a Vibe 5 upgrade, combined with Lebanon diplomatic progress. Lebanon pilot zones Day 3 definitively expired the Rome agreement's original implementation window without confirmed IDF movement — Beirut's explicit threat to skip future Rome talks if Israel does not fulfill its pledge elevates the diplomatic track fragility. Hezbollah stand-down Day 34 holds, signaling Iran prefers continued restraint over declaring the diplomatic track failed, but the implementation momentum has stalled. The PNW fire domain is the session's primary new negative: Kaiser Canyon Fire (Okanogan County / Colville Reservation, 2,170 acres, Level 3 evacuations, 0% containment) and the Franklin County fire complex (~38,000 acres near Kahlotus) represent the first active Level 3 evacuation event of the Eastern Washington burn ban period (Day 3) and the largest new fire complex of the burn ban period, respectively. Both fires are active without containment progress heading into the July 21-24 heat wave peak — the maximum compound risk window for fire growth in Eastern Washington under Super El Niño development and drought Year 4. The measles CDC update (2,260 cases confirmed as of July 16) resolved the prior 'overdue' status and sustains the CIDRAP slowing signal, but the Seafair Fleet Week (T-2, starting July 21) / measles tertiary window (T-4, opening July 23) / next CDC update (~July 23) convergence remains the brief's primary PNW health monitoring scenario. Three primary watchitems for July 20-21: First, Acting DNI Day 59's IC characterization of 72h Iranian restraint — strategic restraint vs. operational pause — is the session's most consequential pending product; the IC conclusion will be the primary determinant of whether oil markets extend their modest Blockade Day 5 relief into a Vibe 5-compatible retracement or sustain the structural IRGC tail risk premium. Second, FERC AI generation adequacy reports (Monday July 20) and Section 301 forced-labor framework finalization (target: before Section 122 expiry July 24) are the session's primary regulatory deliverables — both arrive on Monday during a Blockade Day 5 response assessment period consuming White House bandwidth; USTR non-finalization of the forced-labor framework on July 20 activates the July 20-24 tariff compliance gap window. Third, Kaiser Canyon Fire and Franklin County fire complex trajectory through the July 20 burn-window day — do overnight and Sunday fire crews achieve any containment progress before the July 21-24 heat wave peak, or do both fronts enter the heat wave window without containment, creating maximum compound fire risk conditions? The July 21-24 heat wave peak without containment progress on either front is the primary scenario that would upgrade the local_pnw domain to HIGH stress.
watch_items: Acting DNI Day 59 IC characterization of 72h Iranian restraint — strategic restraint vs. operational pause (July 20): The IC's formal assessment of the 72h absence of confirmed major Iranian kinetic escalation is the session's most consequential pending product. A 'strategic restraint' conclusion — Iran has decided not to escalate kinetically in response to the Hellfire interdiction — is the primary factual predicate for a Vibe 5 upgrade (combined with Lebanon diplomatic progress or WTI retracement below $76); an 'operational pause' conclusion sustains the Vibe 3-4 tail risk and maintains the IRGC energy threat premium. The lapse of the IRGC's explicit 2-3-day ultimatum without triggering is circumstantial evidence of restraint but not confirmation. Acting DNI Day 59 carries this as the primary analytical deliverable alongside the IRGC regional energy intent evaluation.

Lebanon pilot zones diplomatic pathway (July 20-21 — Rome follow-on or Paris channel): The Rome agreement's original implementation window definitively expired July 19 without confirmed IDF movement. Beirut has explicitly threatened to skip future Rome talks. The July 20-21 window is critical: does a Rome follow-on communication extend the implementation timeline with a concrete new schedule? Does a Paris diplomatic channel emerge? Does any IDF movement confirmation arrive in the July 20 business day? An IDF movement confirmation with Lebanese Army control transfer that Iran publicly acknowledges would be the session's most significant diplomatic positive — the factual predicate for Iran to suspend the Hormuz re-closure declaration. A prolonged absence of new diplomatic channel signals risks hardening Hezbollah's assessment that the Rome agreement is non-executable.

Kaiser Canyon Fire + Franklin County fire complex trajectory (July 20 burn window — containment before heat wave peak): Both Kaiser Canyon (2,170 acres, 0% containment, Level 3 evacuations) and Franklin County (~38,000 acres) are active without containment progress heading into the July 21-24 heat wave peak. The July 20 burn window (Sunday into Monday) is the last full suppression opportunity before the heat wave begins to materially accelerate fire growth. Do overnight crews and the July 20 day shift achieve any containment progress — perimeter establishment, flagging, structure protection success? Any containment milestone before the heat wave peak reduces the compound risk scenario. Conversely, both fires entering the heat wave peak without containment milestone is the primary local_pnw Vibe 3 trigger scenario.

FERC AI generation adequacy reports (Monday July 20) and Section 301 forced-labor framework finalization (target July 20-24): Two major regulatory deliverables converge on Monday during Blockade Day 5. FERC generation adequacy reports from all six ISO/RTOs (PJM, MISO, SPP, CAISO, ISO-NE, NYISO) are due Monday — the first national accounting of AI large-load integration readiness; non-compliance by any ISO/RTO moves it toward the August 17 show-cause deadline. USTR must publish the forced-labor Section 301 framework before Section 122 expires July 24 to avoid a compliance gap; White House bandwidth remains consumed by Blockade Day 5. If USTR delays past July 20, the July 20-24 tariff compliance gap window opens for major importers.

Seafair Fleet Week / measles tertiary window / CDC update convergence (July 21-23): Seafair Fleet Week starts July 21 (~500,000 attendance across fleet week); measles tertiary monitoring window opens July 23-26; next CDC measles update (~July 23) is expected the same day as Seafair opening. The July 21-22 pre-Seafair window is the highest-value detection period for identifying any emerging cluster before mass-event attendance peaks. Georgetown wastewater and King/Snohomish ED monitoring are the sole early-detection mechanisms before the CDC data arrival. Confirmed 2,260 total cases (July 16) sustains the CIDRAP slowing signal but does not eliminate amplification risk under the July 21-24 convergence.

Oil price WTI/Brent trajectory — IC characterization as primary catalyst (July 20): WTI ~$78-81 and Brent ~$83-86 are both below their respective Vibe-3 triggers. The primary catalyst for directional movement from these levels is the IC characterization of the 72h Iranian restraint. A 'strategic restraint' IC conclusion released to allies and reflected in market sentiment could catalyze a WTI retracement toward $76 (Vibe 5 oil signal); an 'operational pause' conclusion sustains the current structural premium. The IRGC regional energy threat intent assessment is the secondary price catalyst — resolution in either direction (confirmed operational intent vs. confirmed signaling) would clarify the $85-$95+ risk premium corridor.
